notes.title: Rotund Takeoff Update 1.2
notes.notes:
A number of general Rotund tweaks and fixes have been found since Rotund Takeoff's 1.1 update, so we've brought it up to speed now that both Rotund Rebound and Rotund Zero are concluded!

These are all pretty subtle and technical changes, so the main point of interest would probably be the modernization of the Elite Flag threshold leniency system to match Rotund Rebound and Rotund Zero. Previously we'd set Elite thresholds by taking our dev times and manually adding a bit of leniency while rounding them up to a pretty number. Now they're determined automatically by adding a set leniency to the direct time, making it more consistent and easier to figure what the actual dev time was.

This also means nearly all Elite thresholds in the game have changed by a few frames, mostly for the looser as our previous normal level leniency was roughly 250ms and we've now made it 300ms to match RR. Leaf levels are 1 second and world challenges are 3 seconds.

Also of particular note for PC is that we've updated the project to be built from Unity 2021 instead of 2019, which carries a number of internal implications, and we've dropped x86 support on Windows. This was done for future-proofing and modernizing RT to match the other two Rotund games.

As always, you can check out the full [url=https://www.dahku.com/rotund-takeoff-changelog]changelog[/url] if you're interested in the nitty-gritty. Thanks for playing and we hope you enjoy Rotund Takeoff 1.2!

notes.title: Rotund Takeoff Update 1.1
notes.notes:
It's been a while! That certainly wasn't the plan. The plan [i]was[/i] to swiftly port Rotund Takeoff to Nintendo Switch and release soon after PC. Early test builds looked encouraging, but then we got held up by some pesky technical difficulties that set us back by about two months. Ouch! Happy to report those issues are behind us now, and we've brought the PC up to date with Version 1.1, available right now! To celebrate, it's on sale for the weekend!

[h3]Changelog[/h3]
[i][b]Changes:[/b][/i]
[list]
[*] Replaced the Sleep Bears with new Marvin booths for clarity and consistency.
[*] Lowered the required number of gold medals on the original Marvin booths to match those of the silver.
[*] Moved the Sleep Bears to block the 8-Balls, and they won't move until that world is ranked silver or better.
[*] Due to world map changes, your current position on the world map will be set back to 1-1 after updating.
[*] Changed the medal designs from -, =, and + to stopwatches for clarity and to match Rotund Rebound. Also gave the bronze medal a shine animation.
[*] Game will now run in background when the window loses focus. This can be undone via the registry on Windows, ~/.config on Linux, or Library .plist on macOS.
[*] Tightened 26 Elite Flag thresholds. (1-4, 1-7, 1-B, 1-L, 2-2, 2-3, 2-5, 2-6, 2-L, 3-2, 3-4, 3-5, 3-6, 3-7, 3-L, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3, 4-6, 4-7, 4-L, 5-3, 5-5, 5-6, 5-7, 5-?)
[/list]
[i][b]Minor Changes:[/b][/i]
[list]
[*] 1-4: Added down block near the end for clarity.
[*] Added movement dead zone to level character and world map cursor for hyper-sensitive control sticks.
[*] Rumble option now appears disabled when no rumble support is detected.
[*] Renamed "Assign Gamepad" to "Assign Controller" in the controls menu.
[*] Tweaked Fezawk wing flap sound for less thump.
[*] Corrected World Summary display alignment.
[*] Updated Unity from 2019.4.16 to 2019.4.24.
[*] Updated Rewired from 1.1.38.0 to 1.1.39.1.
[*] Updated TextMesh Pro from 2.0.1 to 2.1.4.
[*] Various internal changes for Nintendo Switch support.
[/list]
[i][b]Bug Fixes:[/b][/i]
[list]
[*] Fixed controller rumbling when game launches.
[*] Fixed incorrect Nintendo Switch controller glyphs.
[*] Fixed title screen breaking from synchronized cancel/confirm inputs.
[*] Fixed allowing button assignment while exiting controls menu.
[*] Fixed potential pixel-perfect display issues (options, title screen, world map).
[*] Fixed quirky Speedrun Clock refresh behavior when enabled mid-game.
[*] Fixed the Speedrun Clock going behind certain bridges on the world map.
[*] Fixed some visual issues while adding the new bear to the Sleep Bears island.
[*] Fixed regular fade-in being visible on world map from opening.
[*] Fixed super rare exception thrown by float zone animation.
[*] Fixed crash when returning from a level in the event data can't be saved.
[/list]

notes.title: Rotund Takeoff Release Day!
notes.notes:
Well, here we are, the big day! It's been quite a while now since Dahku announced our return to game development, but we finally have a new release. After this long, releasing on different platforms, and in an industry that's changed a lot, it pretty much feels like our first release ever. Given that, you'd think we'd have a lot to say on this occasion, but well, we don't really. We're happy with how Rotund Takeoff has turned out, and as a remake it directly shows how far we've come. We're grateful to the small but faithful community that's stuck with us, and grateful to the handful of news sites and influencers who've helped spread awareness.

If Rotund Takeoff looks interesting to you, please do give it a chance! There's a 15% off launch discount for the first week.
We hope you'll enjoy it, and that you'll want to follow along as we continue developing the epic sequel, Rotund Rebound!

notes.title: Release Date + Public Beta
notes.notes:
Sorry it's been a while, but it's no secret that our more frequent updates happen in Discord.

[url=https://discord.gg/Dt9rezQ]https://discord.gg/Dt9rezQ[/url]

If you're not in there already, now's the time; we're running a public beta, so stop in and request a key!

You'll have access to the finished game in its entirety, from now until shortly before launch on [b]January 21st, 2021![/b]

We [i]really[/i] wanted to release Rotund Takeoff this year, but scheduling didn't favor us, so having the full game playable is the next best thing.

We hope to see you there!
